full_judgment:
3. The opposite party Nos. 1-5 contested the case. Their contentions were that the case was not maintainable as one application was filed for pre-empting lands transferred by two kabalas on two different dates-and as such the case suffered from misjoinder of causes of action. And the application was barred by limitation. Their case was that the pre-emptor-petitioner and vendor-opposite party No. 6 are full brothers and they live in the same house. The petitioner also mediated the transfer and had knowledge of the sale from the very beginning of the date of transfer and execution and registration of the kabalas. The patta lands were redeemed and the transferees had been in possession on the basis of the kabalas and the petitioner being a poor man was unable to purchase the land. But he subsequently filed the case at the instance of his son-in-law in collusion with others. 

 5. The opposite party Nos. 1-5 took an appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 23 of 1975 to the Court of the District Judge, Patuakhali, from the order of the learned Munsif. The lower appellate Court dismissed the application for pre-emption holding that one application for pre-empting lands transferred by two kabalas was not maintainable as there was misjoinder of causes of action in view of the provisions of sub-rule 2 of rule 2 of Order 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure and that the application was barred by limitation.
